Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Albuquerque NM
136 AM MST Sat Nov 14 2026

...New SHORT TERM, LONG TERM, AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Issued at 1201 AM MST Sat Nov 14 2026
 
- Slick travel conditions due to valley rain and mountain snow
  will favor the northern half of New Mexico Saturday.

- There is a very low (<10%) risk of flooding impacts over 
  northwestern New Mexico Saturday. 

- Quieter conditions expected Sunday and Monday, with unsettled
  weather returning across western and central New Mexico late
  Tuesday into Wednesday.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Sunday)
Issued at 1201 AM MST Sat Nov 14 2026

The latest water vapor satellite imagery and upper air analysis
show a jet maxima diving southeast from central CA toward AZ/NM.
This jet streak is forecast progress east across NM today, while
carving out an upper low along the NM/CO border. This dynamic
setup will bring a solid round of precipitation that will focus
along/west of the Continental Divide and across the northern
mountains. However, snow levels will be relatively high, generally
8.5Kft or higher. Snow accumulation through this evening will
favor the peaks of the northern mountains, especially the Tusas
Mountains where a Winter Weather Advisory is currently in effect.
Advisory-type amounts will likely show up at ski resort level in 
the Sangre De Cristo Mountains, but impacts will be minimal at 
best. Sufficient instability is forecast this afternoon for some 
thundersnow across the northern mountains, with graupel likely at
the lower elevations. Otherwise, today will be cooler, with high
temperatures 5-15 degrees below average. Expect some improvement
on Sunday as an upper level ridge follows behind the departing
upper low. A backdoor cold front will move into the northeast and
east central plains Saturday night into Sunday with moisture 
trapped in the frontal layer providing a fog setup, which is
showing up in the latest GFS MOS at locales like Clayton and
Tucumcari. Sunday will be warmer west of the backdoor cold front,
but still a few degrees below average for most locales. 

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Sunday night through Friday)
Issued at 1201 AM MST Sat Nov 14 2026

Areas of fog will likely develop Sunday night into Monday morning as
an upper level ridge amplifies over the region and high humidity
remains trapped in the lower boundary layer. Otherwise, Monday
will be warmer most areas, with high temperatures near to 
slightly above average across central and western NM. The upper 
level ridge will shift east of the area Monday night and give way 
to increasing southwest flow aloft and moisture advection Tuesday 
ahead of an approaching upper level trough. The latest model
consensus is for the upper level trough to lift northeast from
AZ/UT and weaken as it moves across CO/NM. However, sufficient
forcing from the upper level trough combined with above average
PWATs across our area will result in a solid round of
precipitation that will favor western/northern NM and especially 
the mountains. Snow levels and amounts will be similar to today's
event and may require an advisory for the Tusas Mountains. Breezy
to windy conditions will come with the upper level trough late
Tuesday into Wednesday, especially across northeast NM in closer
proximity to a deepening lee side trough. Expect a break late
Wedenesday into Thursday, with another potential round of
precipitation by Friday as an upper level low progresses east from
over the Great Basin. However, model spread is still an issue with
this system, so forecast confidence for the end of the week is 
relatively low at this time. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 1201 AM MST Sat Nov 14 2026

Scattered showers will continue through the night, increasing in
coverage across western and northern NM after 12Z. Cigs and vis
will continue to deteriorate over the next 12 hours from the west.
Patchy fog may develop tonight in areas with wet soils, but it 
should be short-lived in most areas. The most persistent MVFR to 
IFR conditions are likely across northern NM between 12Z and 21Z 
tomorrow when the heaviest and most persistent rain/snow showers 
will occur. The NBM is bullish about significant cig reductions 
across western and central areas as well, but it is notably more 
aggressive than MOS guidance. Rain and mountain snow showers 
tomorrow will generally favor areas north of I-40, with lesser 
coverage in southern areas. Snow levels begin around 9.5kft 
tonight, dropping to around 7.5kft by Saturday night. Showers 
taper off from northwest to southeast after 00Z, with only a few 
lingering showers in the northeast by 06Z.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1201 AM MST Sat Nov 14 2026

Critical fire weather conditions are not forecast through at least
the next seven days. High humidity and good chances for wetting
precipitation will prevail through tonight as a developing upper
level low slides east across northern NM. An upper level ridge
will follow with some drying prior to another round of wetting
precipitation late Tuesday into Wednesday as an upper level trough
progresses east across the region. Vent rates will be poor to fair
on Sunday and Monday under the influence of the upper level ridge. 
Another system may bring more wetting precipitation by the end of
next week. 

&&
